used_notes: Yes - the notes changed several calls in both directions: C-10 (nimbus-lite) and C-24 (quarry-pro597) look cross-organisational in the aggregates (5-8 distinct sites, 3-7 regions) but every note that actually names the entity comes from the single loud site R00S02, so I demoted them to artefacts; likewise C-19 (marlin441, 7 'independent sources' on policy_change but only one note ever names marlin441), C-2/C-7/C-18/C-42/C-44/C-45/C-51/C-53 (statistics with essentially zero entity-bearing notes - the counts are background traffic attached to a sibling token such as kestrel-pay vs kestrel-core or zephyr-pay467 vs zephyr-core495), and C-1/C-52 (total_reports far above independent_sources, and the notes show why: one verbatim message re-posted on a single day, d061/d076 for C-1, d033/d047 for C-52); conversely the notes promoted C-33 (arbor-na) and C-28 (basalt-pay458), whose modest counts turn out to be one clean link per region reported in exact causal order.
reasoning_notes:
Method. For each candidate I (a) mapped its links onto the seven causal chains and checked how many links fall on ONE chain and whether their first_seen_day order matches that chain's order; (b) checked that no load-bearing link rests on a single report; (c) read every source note and kept only those that both name the candidate's own entity token and carry a synonym for one of its events - the noisy notes that name a sibling entity (kestrel-pay vs kestrel-core, zephyr-pay467 vs zephyr-core495, granite-pay vs granite-core) are background traffic and do not corroborate the link; (d) read the REGION-SITE-DEPT-TEAM prefix of each corroborating note to see whether the links really come from different parts of the org or from one site repeating itself.

What a genuine one looks like here. C-28 (basalt-pay458) carries the entire chain 5 - firmware_update d21, sensor_drift d30, false_alarm d43, unplanned_downtime d72, output_shortfall d161 - in exact causal order, with the firmware reported out of R01, the drift out of R06, the alarm back in R01 and the downtime in R06; the notes name the entity every time ('firmware pushed', 'sensor readings drifting', 'calibration off', 'spurious alarm', 'asset went down'). C-33 (arbor-na) is the same shape on chain 1: supplier_substitution d18, component_defect d20 (R04S00), yield_drop d30 (R02), shipment_delay d57 (R06), revenue_miss d139 - five links, strictly ordered, each link owned by a different region. C-8 (tundra-core) is the whole of chain 6 in order (d24 price, d34 margin, d54 discount, d66 forecast) with R01/R03/R00/R06 reporting the four links. C-26 (cobalt), C-12 (granite-core), C-27 (basalt), C-25 (zephyr-na), C-17 (solace), C-15 (lumen), C-5 (halcyon) and C-49 (granite) all show 3-5 consecutive links on a single chain, in date order, each link independently sourced from several regions, with entity-bearing notes behind them. C-6/C-32/C-34 do the same on chain 7, C-50/C-55 on chain 3, C-14 on chain 6, C-35 on chain 1.

Why the rejects fail, by failure mode.
- Out of causal order: C-9 (kestrel-pay) is the most seductive decoy - six links, all on chain 1, all richly corroborated by notes that really do name kestrel-pay - but they all land in days 1-5 with the effects before the causes (component_defect d1 and customer_escalation d1 before supplier_substitution d3, yield_drop d5 after shipment_delay d4). That is a co-occurring cluster, not a progression. Same flaw, milder, in C-11 (yield d8 before defect d10), C-43 (unplanned_downtime d79 before sensor_drift d80), C-38 (forecast_revision d80 before margin_compression d81), C-22 (checkout_drop d7 before api_error_spike d10) and C-4 (regulatory_notice d126 before audit_finding d129).
- One loud site: C-10 and C-24 as described above; also C-13 (both links from R01S00-DEPT-06 alone), C-39 (the whole backlog burst is R06 on d037 and both churn notes are R02S01-DEPT-04), C-47 (both backlog notes R06S04).
- Scattered across unrelated chains: C-16 (pellucid-pay456) has seven links spread over four different chains - that is a busy asset, not a risk; C-0 mixes chain-7 links with notes that mostly name quarry-pay rather than quarry-core.
- Links resting on a single report: C-3, C-37, C-45, C-30, C-21, C-46 - impressive n_links, but the chain is held together by 1-source links and almost no entity-bearing notes.
- Statistics with no corroborating text at all: C-7, C-18, C-23, C-29, C-42, C-44, C-51, C-53 - the aggregate counts exist, but no note in the candidate's own evidence ever names the entity alongside the event.

Borderline calls I excluded from 'real': C-54 (halcyon-eu) has four chain-5 links in near-order but all five firmware notes come from R02S01 alone and output_shortfall has no note; C-41 (wexford) is clean and ordered but its middle link (backlog_growth) is a single unsupported report; C-52 (kestrel422) is ordered and well-sourced but is echo-inflated (14/18/7 reports behind 4/10/3 sources) with each link penned into one site; C-36 (wexford-na) is ordered across four links but only two of them are corroborated, both from R01S01. I would hold these for a second week of data rather than put them in front of an executive.
